Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSE 3122/CSE_3122 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  (SPL: COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING)  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [CSE 3122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Apply your knowledge of Systems Engineering to demonstrate how self-driving cars integrate             (5)  
  hardware and software components to achieve autonomous functionality with a suitable diagram.  
  Identify the activity that must be carried out throughout the system development process and apply  
  the same concept to propose two other examples of product development projects where Systems  
  Engineering can be effectively implemented.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               Identify which Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model to be used in the development of           (3)  
  WhatsApp. Explain the life cycle activities of this Model with a diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               Differentiate pair programming in XP from traditional programming with a suitable example.             (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               In a loan processing application with modules like "Verify Applicant", "Calculate Eligibility", and    (5)  
  "Disburse Loan", developers face repeated data validation and unclear module interfaces. As the  
  design lead, explain how you would redesign the system using structured design principles to  
  minimize redundancy and ensure clear communication among modules by highlighting the roles of  
  cohesion and coupling in your solution.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2B)               The SRS for a new banking application is heavily technical and filled with IT Professionals, making    (3)  
  it difficult for non-technical clients to review. Explain how you would modify the SRS structure or  
  language to make it clear and understandable for stakeholders with limited technical knowledge.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)               Imagine your organization is refactoring a legacy payroll application, your team must choose           (2)  
  between improving cohesion first or reducing coupling. Evaluate which should be prioritized and  
  justify your decision.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
3A)               A Smart Travel Recommendation System provides personalized trip suggestions to users. Each             (5)  
  user has a profile with travel preferences (budget, location type, duration). The system maintains a  
  
  Page #1

database of destinations, hotels, and activities. Based on user input, it generates travel packages  
  using an AI-based recommendation engine. Travel agents can upload new package details, and  
  the admin maintains user and booking records. Draw a Class Diagram for this system showing key  
  classes (User, Destination, Package, Hotel, Activity, Admin, RecommendationEngine), their  
  attributes, operations, and relationships.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3B)           A Healthcare Appointment Scheduling System lets patients book appointments with doctors, view         (3)  
  schedules, and receive reminders. Receptionists manage patient records and doctor availability.  
  Draw a Hierarchy Chart (Structured Design) for this system, showing main modules and  
  submodules.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)           Analyze the use of formal methods in software development by examining how their two primary          (2)  
  merits and two major limitations influence the overall software design and quality assurance  
  process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)           Analyse the concept of postscripts to explain how they can be used to improve software                (5)  
  engineering processes in real-world projects.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)           Analyze the workflow of a Hospital Management System by examining how Appointment                    (3)  
  Management, Patient Record Management, and Billing & Inventory Management interact within the  
  system. Using your analysis, design and draw an Activity Diagram that clearly represents the flow of  
  activities across these three components.  
  Appointment Management, Patient Record Management and Billing and Inventory Management.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)           Analyze the state transitions involved in a movie theatre ticket-booking process and use your      (2)  
  analysis to design and draw a State Chart Diagram for the Booking object, showing the states  
  Created, Pending Payment, Confirmed, and Cancelled, along with the events that trigger transitions  
  between them.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)           Analyze the concept of White Box Testing and discuss various coverage-based testing strategies        (5)  
  used in it with suitable examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5B)           Apply various program debugging techniques to identify and resolve software errors that occur         (3)  
  during the development process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)           Analyze the concept of Security Testing and illustrate how it helps identify system vulnerabilities   (2)  
  with a suitable example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
